info.title: rproxy-api control API
info.description: The contract is docs/API.md; this document follows it.

Error.description: Every error response. `code` is stable; `error` is for people.

passthrough.description: terminate rules: relay TLS of these names untouched

targets.description: several backends instead of remote_addr / remote_port (#234): features.tls_route_targets

upstream.description: terminate (tcp) routes that are not passthrough: how to reach this route's backends instead of the rule's tls.upstream (same fields: tls, server_name, ca_file, insecure_skip_verify, cert_file, chain_file, key_file); features.tls_route_upstream

source_ip.description: routes relayed at L4 (passthrough routes of terminate, routes of sni) only: how the client's address is passed to this route's backends, instead of the rule's source_ip (v0.4.13, #297; features.route_source_ip). Left out: the rule's. transparent is per rule; proxy_v1 is tcp only

acme.description: A resolver of global.acme.resolvers (settings file): the certificate is obtained and renewed by ACME instead of cert_file / key_file. Needs the acme:write scope; every name must be in the allowed_names of the resolver's account (and DNS provider), else 400 invalid.

domains.description: Names of the ACME certificate (with acme); *.example.com needs a dns-01 resolver.

cert.description: A certificate stored through PUT /certs/{name} (v0.4.2, #240), instead of cert_file / key_file / acme. Needs the name within the token's allow_certs; a name not stored is 400 tls_config.

mode.description: sni routes by the ClientHello's server name without decrypting: TLS on tcp, DTLS and QUIC on udp

misdirected.description: 421 Misdirected Request when the request's Host is in another group of server name patterns than the TLS server name (http rules with terminate; v0.4.3)

match.description: Traefik rule syntax: Host, HostRegexp, Path, PathPrefix, PathRegexp, Method, Header, HeaderRegexp, Query, QueryRegexp, ClientIP with &&, ||, ! and parentheses.

timeouts.description: #227: the whole request and one attempt to a backend; 0s is no limit (route_timeouts in features.http_options)

status.description: answer with this status instead of url (#235)

middlewares.description: middlewares for this server only (#229): headers, replace_host, strip_prefix, add_prefix, replace_path, replace_path_regex

max_connections.description: requests in progress on this server at most (v0.4.19, #341): a full server is skipped like one that is down; all full is answered 503 (reason target_full). Not with status

tls.description: TLS towards the https:// servers instead of the rule's tls.upstream (#236)

subject_alt_names.description: DNS names or URIs, one of which must be a SAN of the certificate

add.description: appended to an existing value with , (#224)

Middleware.description: Exactly one kind: `{kind: {settings}}`. Kinds this build runs: GET /capabilities features.middlewares.

service.description: instead of address: a service of the rule (v0.4.3)

path.description: with service: the path asked (default /; v0.4.3)

client_request.description: the client's method, path (after the auth path) and Host (v0.4.3)

status.description: answers of these statuses ("500", "502-504") are tried again (#231)

raw_path.description: v0.4.17 (#320): route and forward the path as sent, without normalisation. Unsafe with path-based authentication or ip_allow routes.

strict_path.description: v0.4.17 (#320): answer 400 to paths with %2F, %5C, %3B, %25, ; or a backslash (characters some backends read differently).

Http.description: L7 routing of a tcp rule (plain HTTP or tls.mode terminate).

extra_listen_addrs.description: More IP addresses to listen on with the same port or range (e.g. IPv6 next to an IPv4 listen_addr).

listen_freebind.description: Listen even while the addresses are not on the host (IP_FREEBIND / IPV6_FREEBIND), e.g. a VIP another node holds now (v0.4.3, features.listen_freebind). Cannot change by PATCH.

remote_addr.description: Left out on http rules and rules with targets.

targets.description: Several destinations instead of remote_addr / remote_port (exactly one of them).

connect_timeout.description: How long a connection to a target may take before the next target is tried (tcp without http; 100ms-10m; v0.4.3, features.connect_timeout). Left out: 5s with other targets to fall back on, else the OS's.

crowdsec.description: Refuse clients in the global.crowdsec decisions right after accepting (L4).

targets.description: Several destinations instead of remote_addr / remote_port (exactly one of them).

connect_timeout.description: Replaces connect_timeout when present (0s removes it; left out keeps it).

proxy_protocol.description: Replaces proxy_protocol when present ({} removes it; left out keeps it). Takes effect from the next connection.

crowdsec.description: Refuse clients in the global.crowdsec decisions right after accepting (L4).

extra_listen_addrs.description: Replaces the extra listen addresses when present ([] removes them all; left out keeps them).

listen_freebind.description: Cannot change; accepted only if it matches (like source_ip).

RulePatch.description: The backends (remote_addr or targets, balance, health_check) are replaced as a whole: balance left out is round_robin, health_check left out is none.

services.description: Services with health_check, outlier_detection or a server's max_connections: the state of their servers.

ejected.description: Ejected by outlier_detection (#170); left out when not.

in_flight.description: Requests in progress now; servers with max_connections only (v0.4.19, #341)

full.description: At max_connections now; servers with max_connections only (v0.4.19, #341)

http3.description: Rules with http.http3: whether HTTP/3 (QUIC) is answered on the UDP port, and why not.

dropped.description: UDP datagrams rproxy dropped (a session queue full, or sending failed)

targets.description: Rules with several targets or a health_check, or a target with max_connections (v0.4.19, #341).

tls_routes.description: The targets of tls.routes[] with several targets or a max_connections, in the order of tls.routes (v0.4.19, #341).

limited.description: Refused by limits (v0.4, #165), or because every target was full (reason target_full, v0.4.19, #341)

counters_since.description: When the counters started, Unix seconds; kept over a live upgrade (v0.4, #166)

targets.description: Several destinations; remote_addr / remote_port then hold the first.

proxy_protocol.description: Left out when not set; required is always shown.

origin.description: api: created through the API and stored in rproxy_rules (v0.4, #144); treat unknown values like dynamic

state.description: failed: the rule could not start, or (v0.4.18, #327) it was restored from the database and does not validate: its body as stored, the reason in error, Accepted False (reason Invalid) in conditions; DELETE removes it, PATCH fixes it

all_targets_down.description: Every destination is down (rules with several targets or a health_check; false otherwise) (v0.3.20)

down_services.description: http services with health_check that have no server up; omitted when none (v0.3.20)

crowdsec.description: Refuse clients in the global.crowdsec decisions right after accepting (L4).

cert_status.description: Expiry of the certificates a terminate rule uses (left out when there are none).

acme.description: State of the rule's ACME certificates (left out when there are none).

ruleset.description: The rule set (PUT /rulesets/{name}) that owns the rule (v0.4, #28); left out for other rules. PATCH / DELETE /rules on it is 409 owned.

conditions.description: Gateway API style state (v0.4, #28; features.conditions): every rule, whether in a set or not. state, error, all_targets_down and down_services stay as they are.

created_by.description: Token that created the stored rule (v0.4, #144)

Rule.description: Fields may be added in patch releases.

version.description: The rproxy-api release of this build (Cargo.toml version, e.g. 0.3.18). Added in 0.3.18; absent on older releases

features.description: v0.3 and v0.4 settings this build can run (docs/API.md). In v0.4.0 every boolean is true, middlewares includes geoip, services includes outlier_detection and performance names every key; services includes protocol and tls, middlewares cors, mirror and replace_host

http_options.description: headers_add, redirect_status, route_timeouts, server_middlewares, server_status, retry_status (#224, #226-#235), misdirected (tls.misdirected, v0.4.3), path_normalize, raw_path, identity_headers, http_timeouts, strict_path (v0.4.17, #320)

forward_auth.description: options of forward_auth (v0.4.3): service, grpc, client_request, allow_status, forward_body, all_response_headers

server_middleware_kinds.description: middleware kinds servers[].middlewares may use (#229; cors, redirect_scheme, redirect_regex, mirror since v0.4.3)

client_auth_modes.description: modes of tls.client_auth that can run (optional_no_verify, #238)

performance.description: Keys of global.performance applied from the settings file

ruleset_persistence.description: Rule sets of persist: true tokens are stored in rproxy_rule_sets (v0.4.2)

tokens_reload.description: The token file is re-read when it changes, without SIGHUP (RPROXY_TOKENS_CHECK_SECS; v0.4.2)

listen_freebind.description: listen_freebind of a rule: listening on an address not on the host yet (IP_FREEBIND; v0.4.3)

connect_timeout.description: connect_timeout of an L4 tcp rule (v0.4.3)

proxy_protocol_in.description: proxy_protocol of a tcp rule: PROXY v1 / v2 headers read from trusted front ends (v0.4.13, #296)

route_source_ip.description: source_ip of tls.routes[] relayed at L4: passthrough routes of terminate, routes of sni (v0.4.13, #297)

proxy_protocol_in_udp.description: proxy_protocol of a udp rule: a PROXY v2 (DGRAM) header in front of each datagram from trusted front ends (v0.4.16, #312)

protected_files.description: Rules from the API may not name files of the certificate store, the ACME storage or the settings' secrets (403 protected_file); allow_certs tokens name no file (403 file_not_allowed); an OIDC client secret file keeps to one use (409 secret_reuse) (v0.4.17, #319)

file_owners.description: A token without admin may not name a key or secret file (key_file, client_secret_file, cookie_secret_file, users_file; by inode) that a rule of another owner names: another token's, another token's rule set's, the settings file's, a restored rule's whose creator is not known (409 file_in_use) (v0.4.18, #323)

invalid_restored.description: Rules restored from the database that do not validate are shown in GET /rules with state failed and the reason in error (Accepted False, reason Invalid); DELETE removes them, PATCH fixes them (the PATCH over the stored body, validated as a new rule) (v0.4.18, #327)

global_api.description: GET / PATCH /config/global: the global items the settings file (and the environment) leaves out are set through the API (admin; crowdsec only over the Unix socket by default), stored in rproxy_global and put in force for the next request, connection or UDP session; the file's items win (409 static) (v0.4.19, #342)

target_max_connections.description: max_connections of L4 targets[] (also tls.routes[].targets[]) and of http services' servers[]: a full target is skipped by every balance, all full is refused (reason target_full); max_connections and full in stats.targets[] (v0.4.19, #341)

performance.description: Kernel fast paths (#260, global.performance.xdp): the actual state after the startup test

requested.description: the setting asked for (off when none)

active.description: the fast path is in use (its startup test passed)

reason.description: why it is not used, when requested

build.description: The running binary (v0.4, #174); sha256 is null right after the start

restart_needed.description: global items changed in the file that take effect only after a restart: global.acme, global.geoip, global.performance, global.files (the live items are applied by the reload, #342)

Balance.description: How new connections (sessions, requests) are spread over the destinations.

backup.description: Used only while every other target is down.

max_connections.description: TCP connections / UDP sessions this target takes at once (v0.4.19, #341): a full target is skipped like one that is down by every balance; all full refuses new ones (reason target_full).

ProxyProtocolIn.description: PROXY protocol headers read from the front ends in from. tcp rules: v1 / v2 before the stream (v0.4.13, features.proxy_protocol_in, #296). udp rules: a v2 header of the DGRAM transport in front of each datagram, stripped before it goes on; replies go back to the front end's address and port without a header (v0.4.16, features.proxy_protocol_in_udp, #312). The client of the header is used for allow_from, geoip, crowdsec, limits, bandwidth, logs, X-Forwarded-For and source_ip. A peer outside from that starts with a header is refused (udp: the datagram is dropped). {} means none.

from.description: The TCP peers (CIDR or single IP) whose headers are believed. Required and not empty; /0 is refused.

required.description: Refuse a connection from a peer in from that sends no header. false: without a header the peer's address is used.

port.description: Port to connect to instead of each target's own (required for udp).

max_connections.description: The target's max_connections; left out without one (v0.4.19, #341)

full.description: At max_connections now: skipped for new connections (v0.4.19, #341)

days_left.description: Whole days left; negative once expired.

failed.description: Of the added and changed rules: those registered as failed

restart_needed.description: global items changed in the file that take effect only after a restart: global.acme, global.geoip, global.performance, global.files (the live items are applied by the reload, #342)

CrowdsecStatus.description: The connection to the CrowdSec LAPI (only with global.crowdsec) (v0.3.20)

connected.description: The last pull of the decisions succeeded

synced.description: The decisions have been pulled at least once

last_success.description: Unix seconds of the last successful pull

state.description: pending: not issued yet (a self-signed stand-in is served); renewing: due for renewal; error: the last attempt failed (a certificate issued earlier stays in use)

next_attempt.description: After a failure, or while the rate limit holds the order back

ari.description: The renewal window the CA suggests (ACME renewal information, RFC 9773); renew_at is a random point in it

Acme.description: global.acme: names and states only. Secrets (DNS API keys, EAB keys) and their files are never shown.

helper.description: DNS-01 records are written by the ACME helper (global.acme.helper), which holds the DNS secrets

Labels.description: Free-form marks (owner, tenant, controller), not used for forwarding; keys [A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9._/-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?, values without control characters. PATCH with labels replaces them as a whole ({} removes them; left out keeps them). Shown in the rule.create / rule.update logs and in /metrics as rproxy_rule_labels{rule="tcp/0.0.0.0:443",label_<key with other characters than letters and digits as _>="value"} 1. v0.4 (#28, #166): features.labels

Limits.description: Connection / datagram limits (v0.4, #165): features.limits. {} removes them in PATCH.

max_connections.description: Concurrent connections of the whole rule (UDP: sessions)

Bandwidth.description: Bandwidth limits (v0.4, #166): features.bandwidth. TCP waits, UDP drops. {} removes them in PATCH.

Geoip.description: Country / ASN lists (v0.4, #168): features.geoip (rules) or geoip in features.middlewares. Needs global.geoip databases.

L4OutlierDetection.description: Passive health checks of the targets (v0.4, #170): features.outlier_detection. Not on http rules.

HttpOutlierDetection.description: Passive health checks of the servers (v0.4, #170): outlier_detection in features.services.

Condition.description: One condition of a rule (v0.4, #28), shaped for Gateway API status. Always the four types in this order: Accepted, Programmed, ResolvedRefs, BackendsHealthy.

status.description: Unknown only for BackendsHealthy of a rule that is not running

reason.description: Accepted: Accepted | Unsupported (a setting this build cannot run). Programmed: Listening | BindFailed | Pending (waiting to resolve its targets; retried) | Failed. ResolvedRefs: ResolvedRefs | ResolveFailed | CertificateExpired | CertificateUnreadable | SecretUnreadable. BackendsHealthy: Healthy | AllTargetsDown | ServiceDown | NotProgrammed

last_transition.description: Unix seconds when status last changed (a new reason or message alone keeps it). Programmed True starts at started_at; otherwise a change is noted when the rule is read (GET /rules, GET /rulesets/{name}, PUT /rulesets/{name}). Starts again when the rule is deleted or re-created.

generation.description: The caller's generation (e.g. the Gateway's metadata.generation), stored and returned as is (observedGeneration). A PUT with a lower generation than the stored one is 409 stale_generation.

rules.description: Every rule of the set; each key (protocol, listen_addr, listen_port) at most once.

etag.description: g<generation>-<the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the rules' normalized JSON in key order>; changes when the rules or the generation change, not when their state does

updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the last PUT

updated_by.description: The name of the token of the last PUT (empty without a token file)

owner.description: the token that created the set; only it or an admin token may change or delete it (security review M3)

persisted.description: Stored sets only (v0.4.2, #241): whether the row in rproxy_rule_sets is up to date

updated_at.description: Unix seconds of the last PUT

owner.description: the token that created the set; only it or an admin token may change or delete it (security review M3)

persisted.description: Stored sets only (v0.4.2, #241): whether the row in rproxy_rule_sets is up to date

change.description: For update: in_place (connections kept) or recreate (listeners opened again, connections dropped; also a failed rule started again). none for create, delete and none

state.description: The rule's state after the PUT; left out for delete, dry runs, and a rule whose key was taken by another request meanwhile (error says so)

error.description: Why the rule failed (bind, name resolution)

diff.description: Dry runs, update only: what would change

etag.description: The set's etag after the PUT (a dry run: what it would be); also the ETag header

results.description: The body's rules in their order, then the deleted ones

persisted.description: Stored sets only (v0.4.2, #241): whether the row in rproxy_rule_sets is up to date

RulePlan.description: The answer of a dry run (v0.4, #169)

restart_needed.description: global items changed in the file that take effect only after a restart: global.acme, global.geoip, global.performance, global.files (the live items are applied by the reload, #342)

global_changes.description: global items whose value in force the reload would change (applied by the reload, #342), e.g. global.trusted_proxies

RulesetError.description: A refused PUT /rulesets/{name}: code / error are the first problem (error starts with rules[i]: for a rule's problem), errors lists every problem with a rule (left out when the problem is not about one rule, e.g. stale_generation).

StoredCert.description: A certificate stored through PUT /certs/{name} (v0.4.2, #240). The key is never returned.

sans.description: DNS names (subjectAltName, else the common name)

fingerprint_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the certificate (DER), hex; also the ETag and what If-Match takes

updated_by.description: Name of the token that stored it

warnings.description: PUT only: e.g. it expires within RPROXY_CERT_WARN_DAYS

cert.description: PEM certificate (may hold its chain after it)

key.description: PEM private key (PKCS#8, PKCS#1 or SEC1)

value.description: The value in force (start-only items: as started)

source.description: Where the value in force comes from

apply.description: live: the next request, connection or UDP session takes a new value; restart: read only at the start, not changed by the API

unix_only.description: Changed only over the Unix socket while RPROXY_API_RELOAD_UNIX_ONLY is true: trusted_proxies, access_log, crowdsec (and acme)

settable.description: Whether PATCH may set it now (live and not from the file or the environment; see unix_only for the transport)

api_value.description: The value set through the API (present only when there is one)

shadowed.description: With api_value: the file or the environment sets the item, so the API value is kept but not in force (config.global_shadowed)

error.description: A restored API value that is not in force (refused or not built); it stays stored

kept.description: crowdsec only: the file dropped it, but rules use it, so it stays in force (source file) until no rule does

items.description: By item: trusted_proxies, access_log, crowdsec, http.timeouts, udp_max_sessions (live); acme, geoip, performance, files, control_api (restart)

storage.description: database: API values are stored in rproxy_global (RPROXY_DATABASE_URL); memory: in this process only, lost on restart (kept over a live upgrade)

persisted.description: Whether the row of rproxy_global is up to date (null: no database)

loaded.description: Whether the stored values could be read (false also for a row that does not read); false: PATCH answers 503 not_loaded until the periodic check reads them

applied.description: PATCH only: items whose value in force changed

GlobalPatch.description: The shape of the settings file's global; an item set to null clears the API value (back to the default), [] and {} are values. Each named item is replaced as a whole.

trusted_proxies.description: CIDRs whose X-Forwarded-For is believed; [] trusts none. Unix socket only by default

access_log.description: Absolute path of a file right in RPROXY_API_ACCESS_LOG_DIR (unset: refused); a directory for rproxy's access logs only (pruning deletes files starting with the name); the name may not overlap rproxy's own log or files not of the form <name>.<YYYY-MM-DD>.<ext>. Unix socket only by default

crowdsec.description: As global.crowdsec (lapi_url, api_key_file (absolute), appsec_url, update_interval); swapped in once the new bouncer has pulled from its LAPI. Unix socket only by default (up to 10 s; other changes of global wait meanwhile)

udp_max_sessions.description: The default cap of UDP sessions per rule (RPROXY_UDP_MAX_SESSIONS; 0: none)

items.description: static: the items the file or the environment sets; restart_only: the start-only items named

get.summary: ACME accounts, DNS providers, resolvers and certificates (rules:read); names and states only, never a secret

post.summary: Renew an ACME certificate now, within the rate limit (acme:write; by default only over the Unix socket)

202.description: The renewal is started in the background (see GET /acme)

400.description: Unknown resolver, or names outside the allowlists

403.description: The token lacks the acme:write scope, or the request came over TCP while RPROXY_API_RELOAD_UNIX_ONLY is true

404.description: No rule uses this certificate, or global.acme is not configured

post.summary: Revoke the issued ACME certificate at the CA and order a new one at once (acme:write; by default only over the Unix socket)

200.description: Revoked; a new certificate is being ordered (see GET /acme)

400.description: Unknown resolver, names outside the allowlists, or an unknown reason

403.description: The token lacks the acme:write scope, or the request came over TCP while RPROXY_API_RELOAD_UNIX_ONLY is true

404.description: No rule uses this certificate, it has not been issued, or global.acme is not configured

500.description: The CA refused or could not be reached

post.summary: Create the account at the CA, or find the existing one for its key (acme:write; by default only over the Unix socket)

403.description: The token lacks the acme:write scope, or the request came over TCP while RPROXY_API_RELOAD_UNIX_ONLY is true

404.description: No such account, or global.acme is not configured

500.description: The CA refused or could not be reached

post.summary: Deactivate the account at the CA and set its key aside; the next order creates a new account (acme:write; by default only over the Unix socket)

403.description: The token lacks the acme:write scope, or the request came over TCP while RPROXY_API_RELOAD_UNIX_ONLY is true

404.description: No such account, or global.acme is not configured

500.description: The CA refused or could not be reached

get.summary: Readiness (no token; v0.4, #28). 200 {"ready": true} once the startup restore (settings file, database) is done; 503 while starting or draining (shutting down, or handing over to a new process with #174). A failed rule does not make rproxy unready: rules report their own state in conditions. Use GET /healthz for liveness.
Every rule set (rules:read; v0.4, #28), sorted by name. Rule sets are kept in memory only: after a restart there are none until the controller PUTs them again (wait for GET /readyz).

403.description: The token lacks the scope (rules:read for GET, rules:write otherwise), a rule's listen ports are outside the token's allow_listen_ports, or a rule uses acme certificates without acme:write

get.summary: One rule set with its rules as GET /rules shows them (with ruleset, labels and conditions), in key order (rules:read; v0.4, #28)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The rule set's name: [a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]{0,251}[a-z0-9])?, e.g. k8s/default/web-gateway. Slashes are written as they are (/rulesets/k8s/default/web-gateway); other characters need no encoding.

ETag.description: The set's etag, quoted: "g<generation>-<16 hex digits>" (the body's etag in double quotes)

400.description: invalid: not a rule set name

403.description: The token lacks the scope (rules:read for GET, rules:write otherwise), a rule's listen ports are outside the token's allow_listen_ports, or a rule uses acme certificates without acme:write

put.summary: Apply a whole rule set (rules:write; v0.4, #28)
put.description: Make the set's rules exactly the body's (rules:write; v0.4, #28). Declarative: send the whole set every time; rules of the set missing from the body are deleted. Checked first, all or nothing: the name, the body, If-Match (412), the generation (409 stale_generation when lower than the stored one; equal is accepted), the shape of every rule (400; every problem in errors, the first in code/error as "rules[i]: ..."), rules of the body that overlap each other (400 invalid), conflicts with rules outside the set (409: static for a rule of the settings file, owned for a rule of another set, already_exists for a rule made by POST /rules or an overlap, reserved for the control API's address), the token's allow_listen_ports for every rule created, changed or deleted (403), and the certificate and secret files of every rule created or changed (400 tls_config / invalid). Then: rules left out are stopped first (connections dropped), changed rules are changed in place when PATCH could do it without dropping connections (targets, balance, health_check, timeouts, TLS, allow_from, extra_listen_addrs, http, labels and the other v0.4 settings) and re-created otherwise (port range, source_ip, http on/off), new rules are started, unchanged running rules are left alone, and failed rules are started again. A rule that cannot bind or resolve its targets is registered as failed (state failed, conditions say why) and the rest is applied; the answer is still 200 with the per-rule results. Rules of a set appear in GET /rules with ruleset; PATCH / DELETE /rules on them is 409 owned. Rule sets are not stored in the database. Changes to rule sets run one at a time.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The rule set's name: [a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]{0,251}[a-z0-9])?, e.g. k8s/default/web-gateway. Slashes are written as they are (/rulesets/k8s/default/web-gateway); other characters need no encoding.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Run every check and answer what would change (RulesetApplied with dry_run true, the etag the set would have, and diff for updates) without changing anything (v0.4, #169).

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optimistic concurrency: the request is refused with 412 precondition_failed unless the set exists and its etag is listed. Takes the etag quoted (as in the ETag header) or as in the body, a comma-separated list, W/ prefixes, or * (any existing set).

ETag.description: The set's etag, quoted: "g<generation>-<16 hex digits>" (the body's etag in double quotes)

403.description: The token lacks the scope (rules:read for GET, rules:write otherwise), a rule's listen ports are outside the token's allow_listen_ports, or a rule uses acme certificates without acme:write

409.description: stale_generation / static / owned / already_exists / reserved (nothing changed)

412.description: precondition_failed: If-Match does not match the set's etag, or the set does not exist (nothing changed)

413.description: The body is larger than 32 MiB

delete.summary: Delete a rule set and stop all of its rules at once (rules:write; v0.4, #28)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The rule set's name: [a-z0-9]([a-z0-9._/-]{0,251}[a-z0-9])?, e.g. k8s/default/web-gateway. Slashes are written as they are (/rulesets/k8s/default/web-gateway); other characters need no encoding.

parameters.name: drain_secs
parameters.description: Stop accepting, wait up to this many seconds for the connections of each rule to end (all rules at the same time), then close the rest

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optimistic concurrency: the request is refused with 412 precondition_failed unless the set exists and its etag is listed. Takes the etag quoted (as in the ETag header) or as in the body, a comma-separated list, W/ prefixes, or * (any existing set).

204.description: Deleted (returns once every listener is closed and every connection has ended)

400.description: invalid: not a rule set name, or drain_secs

403.description: The token lacks the scope (rules:read for GET, rules:write otherwise), a rule's listen ports are outside the token's allow_listen_ports, or a rule uses acme certificates without acme:write

412.description: precondition_failed: If-Match does not match the set's etag
